name: Classic Crunch
description: The head's crunch: the preamp just past its middle and the middle up, for open chords and riffs. Put a cabinet after it, such as Boxed Twelves.

name: Clean, Low Input
description: The low input, which passes the input valve by, with the preamp and the master at their tops: clean played softly, a little hair when dug into, and some 10 dB quieter than the others. Put a cabinet after it, such as Boxed Twelves.

name: Cranked Master
description: The preamp at its middle and the master far up, so the power stage clips too and squeezes the chords. Put a cabinet after it, such as Boxed Twelves.

name: Dark Blues
description: A light crunch with the treble and the presence down: a warm, round top for blues. Put a cabinet after it, such as Boxed Twelves.

name: Edge of Breakup
description: The high input with the preamp low: chords that clean up with the guitar's volume and bite when hit hard. Put a cabinet after it, such as Boxed Twelves.

name: Hot Lead
description: The preamp at its top and the middle well up, for single notes that sustain. Put a cabinet after it, such as Boxed Twelves.

name: Rock Rhythm
description: More preamp than the crunch and a little less bass: tight power chords. Put a cabinet after it, such as Boxed Twelves.

name: Scooped Eighties
description: The preamp high, the bass and treble up and the middle down: the scooped rhythm of the decade. Put a cabinet after it, such as Boxed Twelves.
